city.name: Hanoi
summary: Hanoi, capital of North Vietnam since 1954, was a city of under a million people on the Red River. Its centre had three parts: the Old Quarter of narrow shophouse streets north of Hoan Kiem Lake, the French quarter of villas and public buildings to its south, and the government district round Ba Dinh Square, where Ho Chi Minh declared independence on 2 September 1945.

In 1972 much of the population had been evacuated to the countryside. From 18 to 29 December, with a pause on Christmas Day, American B-52s and fighter-bombers struck rail yards, airfields, power plants and depots round Hanoi and Haiphong in Operation Linebacker II, the heaviest bombing of the war.

Bombs fell on the city too. Bach Mai hospital was wrecked on 22 December, and on the night of 26 December a string of bombs destroyed much of Kham Thien street, killing 278 people. North Vietnam put civilian deaths in Hanoi at 1,328. Its air defences brought down 15 B-52s; some of the crews joined the prisoners of war held in Hoa Lo, the 'Hanoi Hilton'.
city.note: Streets are today's from OpenStreetMap, kept only inside the areas built up by 1972; streets are named as they are today, which in Hanoi is mostly as they were then. The Red River, Hoan Kiem and the other lakes are today's OpenStreetMap water; several lakes have since been filled or reshaped, and the river banks were less built over. Landmark outlines come from OpenStreetMap where the building survives; Hoa Lo is drawn as the whole prison block it filled before most of it was demolished in 1993 to 1994, and the Kham Thien bomb damage is drawn as a strip along the street, a simplification of the scattered destruction. Houses between the streets are generated. Map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.

districts.name: Kham Thien street (bombed)
districts.description: On the night of 26 December 1972 a string of B-52 bombs fell along Kham Thien, a crowded street of shophouses south-west of the station. 278 people were killed and 290 injured, and 534 houses were destroyed outright. House 51, where seven people died, is now a memorial.

Kham Thien street (bombed)
properties.description: On the night of 26 December 1972 a string of B-52 bombs fell along Kham Thien, a crowded street of shophouses south-west of the station. 278 people were killed and 290 injured, and 534 houses were destroyed outright. House 51, where seven people died, is now a memorial.

properties.name: Hoan Kiem Lake
properties.description: The Lake of the Returned Sword, at the heart of the old city. Legend says the Le emperor Le Loi gave back a magic sword to a golden turtle here after driving out the Ming in 1428. The Old Quarter lies to its north and the French quarter to its south.

properties.name: Ngoc Son Temple
properties.description: The Temple of the Jade Mountain on an island in the lake, reached by the red The Huc bridge.

properties.name: Turtle Tower
properties.description: A small three-storey tower of 1886 on an islet in the lake.

properties.name: Old Quarter
properties.description: The 'thirty-six streets' of the merchant city, each once named for the guild that worked in it: Hang Bac for silversmiths, Hang Gai for silk, Hang Ma for paper goods. Narrow tube houses, a shop at the front and the family behind round a light well, line every street.

properties.name: Dong Xuan market
properties.description: The big covered market of the Old Quarter, built by the French in 1889.

properties.name: Long Bien (Paul Doumer) bridge
description: A steel cantilever bridge of 1899 to 1902, about 2.4 km long with its approaches, carrying the railway to Haiphong over the Red River. The French named it after the governor-general Paul Doumer.

It was the only crossing of the river in Hanoi and one of the most bombed targets of the war. US aircraft first dropped a span in August 1967; laser-guided bombs cut it again in May 1972 and it was hit twice more that summer and autumn, each time patched and reopened. Anti-aircraft guns were mounted on it.

properties.name: Red River
properties.description: The Song Hong, which floods each summer between high dikes. The dike road marks the eastern edge of the Old Quarter.

properties.name: St Joseph's Cathedral
properties.description: Hanoi's cathedral, consecrated in 1886 on the site of a demolished pagoda, in a Gothic style modelled on Notre-Dame de Paris. Its square towers rise 31 m.

properties.name: Opera House
properties.description: The Municipal Theatre, built from 1901 to 1911 after the Palais Garnier. On 19 August 1945 a Viet Minh rally in the square in front of it began the August Revolution.

properties.name: Hoa Lo prison ('Hanoi Hilton')
description: A prison the French built from 1896 to 1901 for Vietnamese political prisoners, filling a whole block of the French quarter behind high walls.

From August 1964, when Everett Alvarez was brought here after being shot down, North Vietnam held American aviators in it. They called it the 'Hanoi Hilton'. B-52 crews shot down in December 1972 were brought here; the prisoners were released in early 1973. Most of the prison was demolished in 1993 to 1994; the gatehouse is now a museum.

properties.name: Ba Dinh Square
properties.description: The square where Ho Chi Minh read the Declaration of Independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam on 2 September 1945. He died in September 1969; his mausoleum was built on the west side of the square from 1973 and opened on 29 August 1975.

properties.name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
properties.description: Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum, of grey granite, 21.6 m high and 41.2 m wide, built from September 1973 and opened on 29 August 1975, against his own wish to be cremated. It was not there in 1972.

properties.name: Presidential Palace
properties.description: The ochre palace of the French governors-general, built 1900 to 1906. Ho Chi Minh received guests here but chose to live in a small stilt house in its grounds.

properties.name: One Pillar Pagoda
properties.description: A small wooden shrine of the 11th century standing on a single pillar in a lotus pond. It was blown up in 1954 as the French left and rebuilt in 1955.

properties.name: B-52 wreck, Huu Tiep lake
properties.description: Part of a B-52 brought down over Hanoi in late December 1972 fell into this small lake in Ngoc Ha village, where the wreckage still lies.

properties.name: Hanoi railway station
properties.description: The main station, opened by the French in 1902. Its central hall was destroyed by bombing in 1972 and rebuilt in a modern style in 1976; the two wings survive.

properties.name: Kham Thien street
description: A long, crowded street of shophouses, schools and theatres south-west of the station.

On the night of 26 December 1972 B-52s dropped a string of bombs along it. North Vietnam reported 278 dead, among them 91 women and 55 children, 290 injured and 534 houses destroyed outright. A memorial stands at number 51, where a family of seven was killed.

properties.name: Bach Mai hospital
properties.description: Hanoi's largest hospital, founded in 1911, about 1 km from the runway of the Bach Mai airfield.

properties.name: Bach Mai hospital (bombed)
description: On 22 December 1972 a stick of more than 100 bombs from a B-52 fell across the hospital, destroying most of it, operating rooms included, and killing 28 doctors, nurses and pharmacists. Most patients had been moved to the basement or out of the city.
The hospital lay about 1 km from the runway of the Bach Mai airfield, with a fuel depot close by. It was rebuilt, largely with private donations from the United States.
